title: thymus serpyllum subsp. ayachicus
intro: Thymus serpyllum subsp. ayachicus, commonly known as Western Red Thyme, is a subspecies of the Thymus serpyllum species, a type of flowering plant in the mint family (Lamiaceae). Western Red Thyme has been traditionally used for its health benefits, which include its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, making it useful in treating respiratory issues such as coughs and colds, as well as skin problems. The therapeutic actions of this plant include its ability to act as an antiseptic, antibacterial, and antifungal agent, which helps to promote wound healing and prevent infections. The bioactive constituents of Western Red Thyme include thymol, carvacrol, and other volatile compounds, which contribute to its medicinal properties and make it a valuable herb in traditional medicine.
